# Goldman Sachs Interview Experience (Summer Internship, On-Campus)

Last Updated : 11 Jul, 2025

Recently, Goldman Sachs conducted a set of tests in our college in order to select summer interns and I'll try to note my experience in detail here to help others prepare :)
**Round 1:**The first round was an Online Test conducted on the Hackerrank platform. It consisted of 18 multiple choice questions-8 from general Computer Science topics like time complexity analysis, syntax check and formal language and 10 questions on statistics and probability. Scoring: +10 for each correct answer, -2 for wrong answers.
There was also one coding question of 20 marks. The question was as follows: We were given an array of strings which represented the names of cities and 2 more 1-D arrays which represented the x and y coordinates of the cities, in order (So city[0], x[0] and y[0] will have the complete information of the first city). Then we had to answer m queries where for each query we were given a city name and we had to return a city which either had x or y coordinate in common with the current city and had the shortest possible distance from that city. If multiple such cities existed, we had to return the lexicographically smallest one and in case no city had x or y common with the current city, we had to return "NONE".
**Constraints**: n (Number of cities) and m (number of queries)<=10^5
Length of city name<=10
All cities would have unique coordinates.
I used a custom sorting approach and maintained 2 arrays (sort on basis of x-coordinate in one array and y-coordinate in the other, followed by lexicographical order) and then performed a binary search

reported.text: Count the ways to tile a 2xN corridor using 2x1 vertical pieces, 2x2 squares and L-shaped pieces in any rotation, modulo 1e9+7 (N up to 1e6).

sources.passage:
Goldman Sachs OA | 40LPA CTC | 2027 Grad | SDE1
Goldman Sachs operates a next-generation digital vault where confidential financial records are stored inside a secure corridor consisting of 2 × N encrypted storage cells. To comply with regulatory requirements, every storage cell must be assigned to exactly one certified security partition.

The security engineering team has approved the following partition modules:

A Vertical Security Partition covering 2 × 1 cells.
A Square Security Partition covering 2 × 2 cells.
An L-Shaped Security Partition, which may be installed in any of its four rotated orientations.

Each partition must lie completely within the corridor, partitions cannot overlap, and every storage cell must belong to exactly one partition.

Given the length N of the secure corridor, determine the total number of distinct valid partitioning configurations.

Since the answer may be very large, return it modulo 10^9 + 7.

Input Format
The first line contains a single integer N — the length of the secure corridor.
Output Format
Print a single integer representing the number of valid partitioning configurations modulo 10^9 + 7.
Constraints
1 ≤ N ≤ 10^6

Goldman Sachs OA – Questions Asked
Hey everyone! 👋

This platform has given me so much over the years - knowledge, confidence, opportunities, and a community that constantly pushes you to grow. From struggling with basic problems to finally cracking interviews, it’s been a journey I couldn’t have taken alone.

Now it feels like the right time to give back ❤️
If this helps even one person prepare better or feel less lost, it’ll be worth it.


## OA Format
- 2 coding questions  
- Time: 120 minutes  

---

## Question 1 – Matrix Special Elements [Medium]

Given a matrix, count the **distinct elements that are either the minimum or maximum in their row or column**.

**Important constraint:**

- If any **row or column has more than one minimum or more than one maximum**, return **-1**.

---

## Question 2 – Array Burst [Medium]

Given a sequence of characters and a `burstLength`, repeatedly **remove any contiguous group whose size is ≥ burstLength**.

**Key details:**

- Entire group should be removed if size ≥ `k`
- After removal, **new adjacent groups may merge and trigger another burst**
- Continue until **no more removals are possible**

### Example

**Input**

abcdeeeeeddcbfgfhhht
k = 3


**Process**

eeeee → removed
ddd → removed
hhh → removed


**Final Result**

abccbfgft

---
If you’re preparing right now - keep going. It’s tough, but completely worth it.
And when you make it, come back and help someone else too 🤝

Goldman sachs OA question 
# Eliminate Substring 

You are given a string s containing only uppercase English letters. Repeatedly perform the following operation: Remove every occurrence of the substring "AWS" from s After each removal, join the remaining left and right parts of the string Continue until the string no longer contains "AWS". Return the final string. If the final string is empty, return "-1".


 Example 1

```
Suppose s = "AWAWSSG" 
Output: "G" 
```

Step 1: "AWAWSSG" → "AWSG" (removing "AWS" at positions 2-4) 
Step 2: "AWSG" → "G" (removing "AWS" at positions 0-2)


Example 2 

```
Suppose s = "AWAWSS 
Output: "-1" 
```

Step 1: "AWAWSS" → "AWS" (removing "AWS" at positions 2-4)
Step 2: "AWS"→" (removing "AWS" at positions 0-2) Constraints


# Bitwise XOR Subsequences

A subsequence of an array is formed by removing zero or more elements without changing the order of the remaining elements.

In a valid subsequence, each pair of adjacent elements has a bitwise XOR equal to k. Given an array of integers and an integer k, determine the length of the longest valid subsequence. 

Note that any subsequence of length 1 is valid regardless of k, since there are no adjacent elements.

Example 

```
n = 5 
arr:[2,1,3,5,2] 
k = 2 
```

The subsequence [1, 3] is valid because: It has adjacent elements 1 and 3 The bitwise XOR of these elements equals k: 1 XOR 3=2.

There are no longer valid subsequences. For example, [2, 1, 3] is not valid because 2 XOR 1 ≠ 2.

Goldman Sachs Analyst (Software Engineer) Interview
Hello Everyone, Really excited to share my recent interview experience with Goldman Sachs for the Analyst (Software Engineer) position. In total I had to go through 7 rounds (excluding HR), below are the details of each round.


---


# Round 1: Hackerrank online assessment
- 2 medium level interview questions to be solved under 70 minutes.
- Question 1: String compresssion: Given a string with lower and uppercase alphabets return a compressed string as output. ex: aaGGbbbc -> 2a2G3b1c
- Question 2: Vector compression: Given a vector of characters, compress the characters that appear more than equal to a given threshold. ex: a,b,c,c,c,c,b,b,d and threshold = 3 -> final output : a,d


# Round 2: Coderpads round
- This round consists of solving 1 or 2 DSA questions in front of a interviewer. (Just another fancy name for a DSA round)
- Question 1: Given an array arr with heights of dwarfs, return the longest possible array of dwarfs that can be arranged in a strictly increasing order. At any given time, only the dwarf at the start or at the end can be picked. ex: 1,3,4,5,6,3,2 -> 1,2,3,4,5,6
- Question 2: Given a positive number n, return the square root of n without using any inbuit method. The answer should be valid till 2 decimal places.


---


*After the coderpad round, GS has a special series of (3) back to back interviews known as the super day, where every round is an eliminator*

# Round 3: Data Structure
- Started with a brief introduction of the interviewing panel and then me, followed with an in-depth discussion(grilling session) of the current project that I am working on as well as past projects.
- Then a simple DSA queston to find the peak element : https://leetcode.com/problems/find-peak-element/description/ 
- I started with a O(nlogn) approach( yeah, I know I took starting with brute too far), then O(n) and then O(log n).
- Then a follow up question to find an element in the same array, repetation allowed, in case of repetition, return all indexes where the element is found.
- I explained my apporch and the interviewers found it a little complex, but after dry run, they seemed satisfied.
- I was not asked to code anything in this round, the project discussion and the approach and dry run for the DSA questions was enough.

# Goldman Sachs India Hackathon 2026 experience

[Events/Hackathons](/r/Btechtards/?f=flair_name%3A%22Events%2FHackathons%22)

Interesting, 9 rank 1s , obviously on the exact same score, most of them are from andhra pradesh, afaik all are women and most of them are from Shri Vishnu Engineering College for Women. That's some crazy coincidence, damn.

Not only these just search for anyone until top 200/300 ranks, high probability they come from these college itself

Apart from this ,

The hackathon experience was as follows:

It was a 12 hours hackathon,

There were 3 questions, 2 were medium and 1 was hard , each 100 points

Leaderboard was based of score out of 300 , and if tied then time taken to submit was also considered

The hard was actually insanely hard , nobody could pass all the test cases, the best scaled score was 94/100

Towards the end i was trying just to pass all the test cases but couldnt :)

Note: No camera, mic permission were explicitly asked neither was any screen share required,ie, as a participant proctoring wasnt visible, copy paste was also allowed (iykyk) . Hence i feel towards the end it was more of a battle of who had more credits 🤡

There was no dsa based question , all questions were real life based and tested deducing logic on spot after going through the question

Expectations were little different though and i want to see how will those you used unfair means be treated

Other participants please add your insights as well !!!!
